sources.text: The Washington DC metro area — Maryland, Virginia, and DC — is one of the highest-compensating security markets in the United States, driven by the concentration of federal agencies, defense contractors, and government-adjacent commercial tenants who require security personnel with specialized credentials and clearances. Understanding the pay structure and career path in this market is essential for anyone considering a security career here — or transitioning from military or law enforcement. Security Officer Salary Ranges in the DC Metro Area Compensation varies significantly based on armed/unarmed status, clearance level, and contract type. Current market ranges: Unarmed, entry-level, commercial: $16–$22/hr Armed, state-licensed, commercial: $20–$28/hr Unarmed, federal contract (public trust): $22–$30/hr — federal contracts frequently carry Service Contract Act wage determinations that set a floor above commercial rates Armed, Secret clearance, federal contract: $28–$40/hr Armed, Top Secret clearance, federal contract: $35–$55/hr Supervisory positions: Add 20–40% above officer rates depending on scope The Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics publishes current wage data for security guards (SOC 33-9032) by metropolitan area. The Washington-Arlington-Alexandria DC-VA-MD-WV metro consistently ranks among the top five compensation markets nationally for security personnel. The Service Contract Act and Federal Security Pay Federal security service contracts are generally covered by the McNamara-O’Hara Service Contract Act (SCA) , administered by the Department of Labor. The SCA requires contractors to pay at least the prevailing wage and fringe benefits determined by DOL for the specific type of work and geographic location. In practice, this means security officers on federal contracts in the DC Metro earn more than counterparts on commercial contracts for equivalent work — often significantly more when the SCA’s health and welfare fringe benefit rate is included. A federal contract officer earning $28/hr plus the SCA H&W fringe benefit (currently over $5.00/hr) has total compensation well above what a $28/hr commercial officer receives. Understanding this comparison is important when evaluating employment offers. What Federal Security Employers Look for Beyond Licensing Military or Law Enforcement Background Prior military service — particularly military police, security forces, or combat arms — and law enforcement experience are the strongest differentiators for federal security positions. The operational discipline, chain-of-command familiarity, report writing, and situational awareness from these backgrounds translate directly to high-performance federal security work. Veterans transitioning to security careers in the DC Metro have a significant advantage in this market. Active Clearance Status An active clearance — particularly Secret or above — dramatically increases both employability and earning potential. Officers who hold active clearances from prior military or government employment can begin work on federal contracts within weeks rather than months. Maintaining clearance currency is an asset that compounds in value across a security career. Report Writing and Documentation Quality Security incident reports that are clear, factual, timely, and legally defensible are a consistent professional differentiator in the federal market. Contractors who work for high-accountability federal clients have low tolerance for vague, untimely, or inaccurate reports. Supervisors who can identify strong documentation skills in officers and develop that skill in their teams are highly valued. Physical Fitness and Medical Readiness Many federal security positions require passing a physical fitness assessment and maintaining weight and physical standards. Armed positions additionally require maintaining firearms qualification on a defined cycle. Officers who let physical standards or firearms qualification lapse create staffing problems for their employers and risk removal from cleared posts. Career Advancement Path in Federal Security Security Officer: Entry-level post assignment — access control, patrol, incident reporting Armed Security Officer: Requires armed licensing in relevant states, annual firearms qualification, and typically a track record in unarmed assignments first Senior Security Officer / Post Commander: Leads a post team, ensures post order compliance, guides junior officers Shift Supervisor: Responsible for all posts across a shift, officer accountability, incident response, direct client communication Site Supervisor / Project Manager: Overall responsibility for a facility or contract, including staffing, compliance documentation, client relationship management, and quality control Specialized Roles: Risk assessment specialist, personnel security specialist, emergency management coordinator — typically requiring ASIS certifications (CPP, PSP) or emergency management credentials alongside field experience Current Openings at Securemedy Incorporated Securemedy Incorporated is an SBA 8(a), MBE, and DBE certified federal security contractor operating across 16 states, headquartered in Oxon Hill, Maryland. We actively recruit armed and unarmed security officers, site supervisors, risk assessment specialists, and emergency management coordinators across our federal and commercial contract portfolio in Maryland, Virginia, and DC. View all current openings on our Careers page , including positions requiring Secret clearances, supervisory roles in the DC Metro, and specialized assignments tied to our full service portfolio . We offer compensation calibrated to federal SCA wage determinations where applicable, comprehensive benefits (medical, dental, vision, retirement), uniform and equipment provided at no cost, and clear advancement pathways for high-performing officers. We are particularly interested in candidates with active clearances, military or law enforcement backgrounds, and demonstrated performance on federal security contracts. Our track record across federal clients — including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and U.S. Army Barnes Federal Building — reflects the standard we expect from every officer we bring on, and the opportunity that standard creates for career advancement. Frequently Asked Questions Is a security guard license in Maryland valid to work in Virginia? No. Maryland and Virginia have separate licensing regimes with no automatic reciprocity. Working an armed or unarmed security post in Virginia requires separate DCJS registration, including completion of Virginia’s Entry Level Training requirement. Officers who hold Maryland registration need to complete Virginia’s licensing process before working any Virginia assignment. What is the fastest way to increase my earning potential as a security officer in the DC area? Two paths are most impactful: obtaining armed licensure in all three jurisdictions (Maryland, Virginia, and DC) and pursuing clearance eligibility if you have a qualifying background. Armed federal contract officers with active Secret clearances represent the highest-compensated segment of the uniformed security workforce in this market, and that population is consistently undersupplied relative to demand. Do security companies in DC provide training to help officers get armed licenses? Reputable security companies — including Securemedy — sponsor officers through the training and licensing process for armed endorsements in the jurisdictions where they operate. If an employer is not willing to invest in your licensing in return for a reasonable service commitment, that is a signal about how they view their workforce. Companies that invest in officer credentials have lower turnover and better operational performance — which is why we do it. We are particularly interested in candidates with active clearances, military or law enforcement backgrounds, and demonstrated performance on federal security contracts. Our track record across federal clients — including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and U.S. Army Barnes Federal Building — reflects the standard we expect from every officer we bring on, and the opportunity that standard creates for career advancement. Frequently Asked Questions Is a security guard license in Maryland valid to work in Virginia? No. Maryland and Virginia have separate licensing regimes with no automatic reciprocity. Working an armed or unarmed security post in Virginia requires separate DCJS registration, including completion of Virginia’s Entry Level Training requirement. Officers who hold Maryland registration need to complete Virginia’s licensing process before working any Virginia assignment. What is the fastest way to increase my earning potential as a security officer in the DC area? Two paths are most impactful: obtaining armed licensure in all three jurisdictions (Maryland, Virginia, and DC) and pursuing clearance eligibility if you have a qualifying background. Armed federal contract officers with active Secret clearances represent the highest-compensated segment of the uniformed security workforce in this market, and that population is consistently undersupplied relative to demand. Do security companies in DC provide training to help officers get armed licenses? Reputable security companies — including Securemedy — sponsor officers through the training and licensing process for armed endorsements in the jurisdictions where they operate. If an employer is not willing to invest in your licensing in return for a reasonable service commitment, that is a signal about how they view their workforce. Companies that invest in officer credentials have lower turnover and better operational performance — which is why we do it. Opting in ensures you receive timely, direct updates regarding your application status, interview schedules, and essential onboarding steps without having to constantly check your email. Opt-Out: I have the right to opt-out of receiving SMS messages from Securemedy at any time. Privacy: Securemedy will treat my personal information and phone number with the utmost confidentiality and will not share it with third parties except as required by law or as necessary for recruitment purposes. For more details, please refer to our Privacy Policy. Additional Options If you do not wish to receive SMS messages, you can choose not to check the SMS consent box on our forms. I have read and understood the terms and conditions outlined in this SMS consent form, and I voluntarily provide my consent to receive SMS messages from Securemedy for recruitment-related purposes.

sources.title: $5,000 Image Excellence Challenge – Securemedy Nigeria Limited
sources.text: $5,000 Image Excellence Challenge Rewarding our security personnel for their professional appearance August 1, 2024 - August 31, 2024. Our Objective The purpose of this challenge is to motivate and reward our security personnel for maintaining and enhancing their professional appearance, which reflects the company's commitment to excellence and professionalism at all worksites. Prize Categories 1st place First Place: $5,000 Our top prize! This substantial reward goes to the security personnel who best exemplifies our standards of professionalism and excellence. 2nd place Second Place: $2,500 Still a significant reward, the second place prize is for the personnel who comes close to meeting the high bar set by our first place winner. 3rd place Third Place: $1,000 Recognition for your commitment to maintaining a professional appearance, the third place prize is our way of saying 'well done!' Eligibility Criteria Open to all uniformed security personnel employed by the company and in good standing Evaluation Criteria Uniform Neatness and Fit We're looking for security personnel who wear their uniforms with pride. Your uniform should be properly fitted, clean, and well-maintained. Grooming Personal grooming is a key part of professional appearance. Compliance with our grooming policy is essential, which includes aspects like hair, facial hair, nails, and personal hygiene. Professionalism Professionalism isn't just about how you look, it's also about how you act. We'll be evaluating your posture, communication, and conduct. Consistency Consistency is key in this challenge. We're looking for security personnel who maintain high appearance standards throughout the contest period. Note: Eligible participants must meet ALL the mandatory requirements as outlined in CEO Directive_ CD 007.1 Image and Appearance Standards (NO EXCEPTIONS!!!) CEO DIRECTIVE CD_007 Image and Appearance Standards Contest Period The $5,000 Image Excellence Challenge takes place from August 1, 2024, to October 31, 2024. During this 3-month period, participants must register, maintain a professional appearance, and be evaluated by a judging panel. Winners will be announced after October 31, 2024. Entry Process 01 Step #1 Participants must complete a registration form. 02 Step #2 Registration must include 2 clear pictures of officer in uniform (head to toe) including: Front View & Rear View 03 Step #3 Registration, with pictures to be submitted via email to admin@securemedy.com by Friday, August 30, 2024, at 5:00pm Extra Credit Exercise To improve chances of selection, eligible applicants may submit a 1-paragraph, brief statement outlining their approach to maintaining their professional appearance. EXTRA CREDIT Judging Process Evaluating Excellence Panel of corporate management judges to evaluate entries based on the criteria listed. Behind the Scenes Judge(s) will conduct random in-person site visits to observe participants on work site Deciding the Best Judges will select the highest rated candidates (all criteria met) for consideration of prizes From Submission to Selection Final selections to be made no later than November 30, 2024, by 5:00pm The Path to Victory Winners to be announced during upcoming 15-year Anniversary Employee Appreciation Gala Registration Form Contact Information For any questions or further information, please contact Ms. Unique Brooks, Office Administrator Telephone +1 240-419-3125 Email Address admin@securemedy.com

sources.title: Emergency Management – Securemedy Nigeria Limited
sources.text: Specialized Division Emergency Management Our Emergency Management division builds and exercises continuity of operations (COOP) plans, coordinates disaster response mobilization, and supports FEMA-aligned emergency planning for federal agencies and commercial campuses. The goal in every engagement is the same: minimize downtime and protect people when a disruptive event hits. Planning work is paired with hands-on exercises — not just a binder on a shelf. We run tabletop exercises and full-scale drills so that the plan has actually been tested by the people who will execute it, and we staff Emergency Operations Centers (EOCs) during activations when clients need experienced hands managing the response.
